statements.text: It is absolutely critical to our national security that we stay ahead of our near-peer adversaries, particularly China, so that we maintain our superior advantage.
statements.context: Opening remarks by Rep. Hudson at a House hearing on AI technology, energy infrastructure, and U.S. global competitiveness.

statements.text: while advancement of AI has so much potential to improve efficiencies across many industries, it can also be used maliciously and cause serious damage. While we have seen a few instances of placing measured safeguards on certain uses of AI, we must balance any regulation with enabling innovation.
statements.context: Subcommittee hearing on AI applications in communications and technology, during the member's five-minute questioning period.

statements.text: Our adversaries will stop at nothing to undermine our leadership in technological advancement and utilize AI to threaten our way of life. We must continue to innovate and develop to prevent that from happening. Competition in AI is a global issue, and it is imperative that the United States maintains its leadership.
statements.context: House Energy & Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology hearing opening statement by Chairman Richard Hudson.

statements.text: Well, I appreciate that, and that is just one more reason we have got to win the race to develop AI. You know, we have got to be the ones with the best systems.
statements.context: Opening statement by Rep. Frank Pallone at a legislative hearing on communications network security before a House Energy & Commerce subcommittee.
